Matching the Stock Synthesis configuration: Indian Ocean yellowfin

Setup 
library(opal)
library(ggplot2)

data(io_yft_data)
data(io_yft_parameters)
data(io_yft_map)
data(io_yft_reference)

ref  <- io_yft_reference
d    <- io_yft_data
n_ts <- d$n_year
sf   <- ref$ss3$sizefreq

# Model outputs precomputed by data-raw/generate-io-yft-vignette-cache.R
cache <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "io_yft_vignette_cache.rds", package = "opal"))
m <- cache$models

fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")
fleet_name <- function(f) sprintf("%d: %s", as.integer(f), ref$fleet_names[as.integer(f)])
last <- function(df, v) df[[v]][df$ts == max(df$ts)]

series_col <- c("opal C2 (length)" = "#1E8449", "opal AGE" = "#8E44AD",
                "opal AGE-NP" = "#2E86C1", "opal AGE-NP-SF" = "#D35400",
                "opal AGE-SF" = "#C2185B",
                "SS3" = "grey20", "Simulated truth" = "#D4AC0D")
series_lty <- setNames(rep("solid", length(series_col)), names(series_col))
series_lty[["opal AGE-NP"]] <- "42"
series_lty[["opal AGE-SF"]] <- "42"
scale_series <- list(scale_colour_manual(values = series_col, name = NULL, drop = TRUE),
                     scale_linetype_manual(values = series_lty, name = NULL, drop = TRUE))
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

Two earlier articles fitted opal to the simulated Indian Ocean yellowfin data and compared it with the Stock Synthesis (SS3) model of the same data: vignette("io-yft-ss3-comparison", package = "opal") (length-based selectivity, fit C2) and vignette("io-yft-age-selectivity", package = "opal") (SS3’s age-based selectivity curves, fits A and A-SS3). This article starts from that article’s fit A-SS3, called AGE here: it uses SS3’s selectivity basis, curve families and mirrors, and estimates every selectivity parameter SS3 estimated, including the index’s logistic curve. (No opal fit here has SS3 in its name; “SS3” always means the Stock Synthesis model.) Two SS3 settings remained that opal could not represent until now. This article adds them, one at a time:

  • AGE-NP (“no priors”) switches off the priors, as SS3’s control file does with a lambda of 0 on parameter priors.
  • AGE-NP-SF (“no priors, size frequency”) also fits SS3’s generalised size compositions for the index (the longline survey, fleet 17), on SS3’s own size bins, with SS3’s lambda of 0.51. This is the model with SS3’s configuration.

A third fit, AGE-SF, keeps opal’s default priors and adds only the index size compositions to AGE. It separates the effect of the size data from that of the priors, and with the priors every selectivity parameter is identifiable.

What SS3 does that AGE does not

SS3’s control file changes two lambdas from their default of 1:

Show code 
knitr::kable(ref$ss3$lambdas[, c("like_comp", "component", "fleet", "value")],
             col.names = c("SS3 code", "Component", "Fleet", "Lambda"))
SS3 code Component Fleet Lambda
11 parameter priors 1 0.00
6 size frequency 17 0.51

opal now takes both. The prior entry of data$lambdas scales the prior term, and opal can fit composition data on bins that differ from row to row (prep_lf_data() with a list of wide tables), each with an lf lambda by fleet.

Some structural differences remain, as accepted differences rather than settings to match:

SS3 (this model) opal (AGE-NP, AGE-NP-SF)
Timing within the quarter Catch by hybrid F (Baranov), index and compositions at mid-quarter Catch removed at the start of the quarter; everything evaluated at the start
Index catchability One series, one analytic q Four quarterly series, four estimated q
Recruitment deviations Sum to zero (do_recdev = 1) Unconstrained
Recruitment age Age 0 at t Age 1 at t + 1
Selectivity bounds Per parameter (index inflection 8–18 quarters) ±20 on opal’s age scale for every par_sel

Step 1: no priors

opal’s IO yellowfin inputs carry the default priors from get_priors(): N(0, 2) on every par_sel element and weak normal priors on log B0 and the catchabilities. SS3 has none, so AGE-NP sets the prior lambda to 0:

Show code 
# In the opal repository: data-raw/io-yft-ss3-matched-setup.R
source("data-raw/io-yft-ss3-matched-setup.R")
inputs <- io_yft_matched_inputs()

d_s1 <- inputs$data                    # AGE's data: sel_basis_f = 2
d_s1$lambdas <- list(prior = 0)

At AGE’s estimates the prior term is 678.7 likelihood units, so it is not a small part of AGE’s objective. Removing it exposes parameters the data do not inform. With every selectivity parameter SS3 estimated, the Hessian of AGE-NP has 10 near-zero eigenvalues: the likelihood is flat in those directions.

Show code 
fl <- cache$s1_free$flat
col_name <- c("peak", "plateau", "ascending width", "descending width")
held <- fl[fl$held, ]
held_tab <- aggregate(col ~ fishery, held, function(x) paste(col_name[x], collapse = ", "))
held_tab$fishery <- fleet_name(held_tab$fishery)
knitr::kable(held_tab, col.names = c("Fishery", "Held fixed"),
             caption = sprintf("The %d selectivity parameters held fixed in AGE-NP.", nrow(held)))
The 20 selectivity parameters held fixed in AGE-NP.
Fishery Held fixed
1: fishing_gi_1 plateau
2: fishing_gi_4 plateau, ascending width
3: fishing_hd_1 plateau, ascending width
4: fishing_ll_1 plateau, descending width
5: fishing_ll_2 plateau, descending width
6: fishing_ll_3 plateau
7: fishing_ll_4 plateau, descending width
8: fishing_other_1 plateau
9: fishing_other_4 descending width
10: fishing_bb_1 ascending width
11: fishing_ps_1 plateau
12: fishing_ps_2 plateau
13: fishing_ps_4 plateau, descending width
14: fishing_trol_1 ascending width

They fall into three groups. The plateau width of the dome-shaped fisheries is very negative, so the plateau is a single age and any lower value gives the same curve. Several ascending (and fishery 9’s descending) limbs are knife-edge, so making them steeper changes nothing. And the asymptotic fisheries 4, 5, 7 and 13 reach full selectivity before the oldest ages, so their plateau and descending limb are not seen at all; C2 fixes the same parameters for the same reason. Under the prior, these parameters sat at the prior’s mean. Without it they drift, and the fit cannot be checked. AGE-NP and AGE-NP-SF hold them at their values in the free fit, which leaves the objective unchanged and 38 of SS3’s 58 selectivity parameters estimated (AGE-NP-SF: 38). SS3 estimated all 58, but was run without a Hessian (Report.sso has none), so it never tested whether they were identified.

Step 2: the index size compositions

SS3’s generalised size compositions for the survey use 14 bins with lower edges 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160 cm, in numbers, 127 observations with sample sizes of 5–35. SS3’s SIZEFREQ_TRANSLATION table in Report.sso puts the population below 30 cm into the first bin, and the last bin is open-ended. opal’s default "accumulate" tails do both. In opal the index is four quarterly series, so each observation goes to the index fishery of its quarter; the four share one selectivity curve, as SS3’s survey does.

Show code 
# The bundled 5 cm compositions and SS3's size compositions, each as a wide
# table of counts (proportion x sample size). The size bins end at the top of
# the model's length grid.
top <- d_s1$len_bin_start + d_s1$n_len * d_s1$len_bin_width
d_s2 <- prep_lf_data(
  inputs$data,
  list(io_yft_lf_wide(inputs$data), io_yft_sizefreq_wide(io_yft_reference)),
  lf_switch = 1L, lf_var_adjust = inputs$data$lf_var_adjust,
  lf_addtocomp = inputs$data$lf_addtocomp, lf_upper_edge = c(top, top))

# SS3's lambdas: 0 on priors, 0.51 on the survey's size compositions
lf_lambda <- rep(1, d_s2$n_fishery)
lf_lambda[17:20] <- io_yft_reference$ss3$sizefreq$lambda
d_s2$lambdas <- list(prior = 0, lf = lf_lambda)

Only opal’s predictions are rebinned: the observations stay on SS3’s bins. At SS3’s solution (before fitting), opal’s predicted size compositions are close to SS3’s expected values:

Show code 
ss3_like <- function(o, e, n) { i <- o > 0; -sum(n[i] * o[i] * log(e[i] / o[i])) }
sf_pred <- function(nm) merge(sf$data, m[[nm]]$sizefreq, by = c("fishery", "ts", "bin"))
chk <- sf_pred("S2_start")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("Largest difference in a proportion", "Mean absolute difference",
               "SS3-style multinomial likelihood, SS3's expected values",
               "The same, opal's predictions", "SS3's reported likelihood (Report.sso)"),
  value = c(fmt(max(abs(chk$predicted - chk$expected)), 4),
            fmt(mean(abs(chk$predicted - chk$expected)), 4),
            fmt(ss3_like(chk$obs, chk$expected, chk$nsamp), 1),
            fmt(ss3_like(chk$obs, chk$predicted, chk$nsamp), 1), "1,067.4")),
  col.names = c("At SS3's solution", "Value"))
At SS3’s solution Value
Largest difference in a proportion 0.0102
Mean absolute difference 0.0014
SS3-style multinomial likelihood, SS3’s expected values 1,067.5
The same, opal’s predictions 1,064.0
SS3’s reported likelihood (Report.sso) 1,067.4

The remaining difference is the timing: SS3 takes the survey at mid-quarter, opal at the start. (The SS3-style likelihood is −Σ N o log(e / o); opal’s multinomial differs by a constant, so its own values are larger.)

Fits

Show code 
fits <- list("opal C2 (length)" = m$C2, "opal AGE" = m$A_ss3,
             "opal AGE-NP" = m$S1, "opal AGE-NP-SF" = m$S2,
             "opal AGE-SF" = m$S3)
fit_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(nm) {
  x <- fits[[nm]]
  w <- if (is.null(x$nll_w)) c(x$nll[c("index", "length")], sizefreq = 0,
                               x$nll[c("recruitment", "prior")]) else x$nll_w
  data.frame(model = nm, sel = x$sel_free, n_par = x$fit$n_par, objective = x$objective,
             index = w[["index"]], length = w[["length"]], sizefreq = w[["sizefreq"]],
             rec = w[["recruitment"]], prior = w[["prior"]],
             grad = formatC(x$fit$max_gradient, format = "e", digits = 1),
             check = if (isTRUE(x$fit$passes)) "passed" else "failed")
}))
knitr::kable(fit_tab, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Model", "Selectivity parameters", "Estimated parameters",
                           "Objective", "Index", "Length comps", "Index sizes (× 0.51)",
                           "Recruitment", "Priors", "Max |gradient|", "opal_check()"))
Model Selectivity parameters Estimated parameters Objective Index Length comps Index sizes (× 0.51) Recruitment Priors Max |gradient| opal_check()
opal C2 (length) 49 310 14406.6 -240.3 14236.2 0.0 136.3 444.4 8.0e-12 passed
opal AGE 58 319 14625.3 -240.2 14220.6 0.0 136.9 678.7 1.2e-11 passed
opal AGE-NP 38 299 13936.8 -240.5 14214.0 0.0 137.3 0.0 3.2e-03 failed
opal AGE-NP-SF 38 299 14912.4 -237.3 14225.0 968.7 136.3 0.0 1.2e-01 failed
opal AGE-SF 58 319 15602.0 -237.1 14231.6 969.2 136.1 679.4 7.0e-12 passed

The objectives are not comparable across rows: each step changes what the objective contains. All three new fits start from AGE’s estimates and converge (nlminb, then Newton steps only where they improve the fit). AGE-SF, with the priors, passes opal_check(). AGE-NP does not: its Hessian is positive definite, but the largest gradient (3.2e-03) is above the strict tolerance of 1e-4 used for these fits. AGE-NP-SF does not either: its Hessian is not positive definite, so without a prior some remaining selectivity directions are only weakly determined once the index size compositions are added. The point estimates of AGE-NP and AGE-NP-SF are usable for comparison with SS3, but AGE-NP-SF’s standard errors are not. SS3, run without a Hessian, gives no information on this.

Starting values

Started from SS3’s own solution instead, opal stops at a different optimum. The fits below use the same data and map as AGE-NP and AGE-NP-SF and differ only in where they start: SS3’s solution, the other model’s estimates (the cross start), and four jitters of AGE’s estimates (normal, SD 0.2, on the estimated selectivity parameters and log B0). They are not polished, so objectives within about 0.01 are the same optimum.

Show code 
st <- cache$starts
start_lab <- c(ss3 = "SS3's solution", cross = "Cross start",
               jitter1 = "Jitter 1", jitter2 = "Jitter 2",
               jitter3 = "Jitter 3", jitter4 = "Jitter 4")
st_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(st$jobs)), function(i) {
  r <- st$runs[[i]]
  ref_fit <- st$reference[[st$jobs$model[i]]]
  if (!is.null(r$error)) return(data.frame(model = st$jobs$model[i],
    start = start_lab[[st$jobs$start[i]]], dobj = NA, B0 = NA, dep = NA))
  data.frame(model = st$jobs$model[i], start = start_lab[[st$jobs$start[i]]],
             dobj = r$objective - ref_fit$objective, B0 = r$B0 / ref$ss3$ssb0,
             dep = tail(r$static_dep, 1))
}))
ref_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(st$reference), function(nm) data.frame(
  model = nm, start = "AGE's estimates (as fitted)", dobj = 0,
  B0 = st$reference[[nm]]$B0 / ref$ss3$ssb0, dep = tail(st$reference[[nm]]$static_dep, 1))))
st_tab <- rbind(ref_rows, st_tab)
st_tab <- st_tab[order(st_tab$model), ]
st_tab$model <- c(S1 = "AGE-NP", S2 = "AGE-NP-SF")[st_tab$model]
knitr::kable(st_tab, digits = c(0, 0, 2, 3, 3), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Model", "Start", "Objective − fitted", "B0 / SS3 B0",
                           "Terminal SSB / B0"))

st_traj <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(st$jobs)), function(i) {
  r <- st$runs[[i]]
  if (!is.null(r$error)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(ts = seq_len(n_ts), dep = r$static_dep, model = st$jobs$model[i],

}))
fit_traj <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(st$reference), function(nm)
  data.frame(ts = seq_len(n_ts), dep = st$reference[[nm]]$static_dep, model = nm)))
ss3_traj <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(st$reference), function(nm)
  data.frame(ts = ref$ss3$trajectory$ts, dep = ref$ss3$trajectory$static_dep, model = nm)))
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = st_traj, aes(ts, dep, colour = start), linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = fit_traj, aes(ts, dep), colour = series_col[["opal AGE-NP-SF"]],
            linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_line(data = ss3_traj, aes(ts, dep), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 1,
             labeller = as_labeller(c(S1 = "AGE-NP", S2 = "AGE-NP-SF"))) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "Start", end = 0.85) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = "Time step (quarter)", y = "SSB / B0")
Show code 
ss3_row <- st_tab[st_tab$start == "SS3's solution", ]

From SS3’s solution, both AGE-NP and AGE-NP-SF stop at an optimum 20.9–22.0 likelihood units worse than the fits started from AGE’s estimates, with B0 0.96–1.02 × SS3’s. That optimum is close to SS3 in stock size, but opal’s data fit prefers the other. The jittered starts show how stable the fitted optimum is: those that return to it (objective difference near 0) give the same stock status. The likelihood surface without priors has more than one optimum, so a comparison of stock size with SS3 depends on where each model starts.

Selectivity

Show code 
sel_series <- c("opal AGE", "opal AGE-NP", "opal AGE-NP-SF",
                "opal AGE-SF")
sa <- rbind(
  data.frame(ref$ss3$sel_age, series = "SS3"),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(sel_series, function(nm) data.frame(fits[[nm]]$sel_age, series = nm))))
sa$series <- factor(sa$series, names(series_col))
ggplot(sa[sa$fishery <= 17, ], aes(age, sel, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 4, labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Selectivity")
Show code 
a50 <- function(sa) {
  s <- sa[sa$fishery == 17, ]
  stats::approx(s$sel, s$age, 0.5, ties = "ordered")$y
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  model = c("SS3", sel_series),
  a50 = c(a50(ref$ss3$sel_age), vapply(sel_series, function(nm) a50(fits[[nm]]$sel_age),
                                       numeric(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE))),
  digits = 2, col.names = c("Model", "Index: age at 50% selectivity (quarters)"))
Model Index: age at 50% selectivity (quarters)
SS3 8.14
opal AGE 8.50
opal AGE-NP 8.47
opal AGE-NP-SF 8.28
opal AGE-SF 8.32

Fisheries 15 and 16 mirror 14, and panel 17 stands for all four quarterly index series. Without the size compositions (AGE, AGE-NP), the index selectivity is informed only by the CPUE trend. With them (AGE-NP-SF, AGE-SF) its age at 50% selectivity moves towards SS3’s. SS3’s estimate sits at its lower bound of 8 quarters, which opal does not impose.

Fits to the data

Index size compositions

Show code 
agg_sf <- function(p, v) {
  a <- tapply(p[[v]] * p$nsamp, p$bin, sum)
  data.frame(bin = as.numeric(names(a)), value = as.numeric(a / sum(a)))
}
p_s2 <- sf_pred("S2")
p_a <- sf_pred("A_ss3_S2")
p_s3 <- sf_pred("S3")
obs_sf <- agg_sf(p_s2, "obs")
lines_sf <- rbind(data.frame(agg_sf(p_s2, "expected"), series = "SS3"),
                  data.frame(agg_sf(p_a, "predicted"), series = "opal AGE"),
                  data.frame(agg_sf(p_s2, "predicted"), series = "opal AGE-NP-SF"),
                  data.frame(agg_sf(p_s3, "predicted"), series = "opal AGE-SF"))
lines_sf$series <- factor(lines_sf$series, names(series_col))
ggplot() +
  geom_col(data = obs_sf, aes(bin + 5, value), fill = "grey80", width = 10) +
  geom_line(data = lines_sf, aes(bin + 5, value, colour = series, linetype = series),
            linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Length (cm; the last bin is 160 cm and above)", y = "Proportion")

Stock status

Show code 
traj <- rbind(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(nm) data.frame(fits[[nm]]$trajectory, series = nm))),
  data.frame(ref$ss3$trajectory, series = "SS3"),
  data.frame(ref$truth$trajectory, series = "Simulated truth"))
traj$series <- factor(traj$series, names(series_col))
long <- rbind(data.frame(ts = traj$ts, series = traj$series, value = traj$ssb / 1e6,
                         panel = "Spawning biomass (million t)"),
              data.frame(ts = traj$ts, series = traj$series, value = traj$static_dep,
                         panel = "SSB / B0"))
ggplot(long, aes(ts, value, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +

Show code 
ss3_tr <- ref$ss3$trajectory
vs_ss3 <- function(tr) {
  mm <- merge(tr, ss3_tr, by = "ts")
  c(mean_pct = mean(abs(100 * (mm$ssb.x / mm$ssb.y - 1))),
    max_dep = max(abs(mm$static_dep.x - mm$static_dep.y)))
}
status <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(nm) {
  x <- fits[[nm]]
  data.frame(model = nm, B0_ss3 = x$B0 / ref$ss3$ssb0, B0_truth = x$B0 / ref$truth$b0,
             dep = last(x$trajectory, "static_dep"), t(vs_ss3(x$trajectory)))
}))
status <- rbind(status,
  data.frame(model = "SS3", B0_ss3 = 1, B0_truth = ref$ss3$ssb0 / ref$truth$b0,
             dep = last(ss3_tr, "static_dep"), mean_pct = NA, max_dep = NA),
  data.frame(model = "Simulated truth", B0_ss3 = ref$truth$b0 / ref$ss3$ssb0, B0_truth = 1,
             dep = last(ref$truth$trajectory, "static_dep"), mean_pct = NA, max_dep = NA))

AGE-NP-SF off (λ = 0) yes (λ = 0.51) the identifiable ones
AGE-SF opal defaults yes (λ = 0.51) all 58

dep <- function(nm) last(fits[[nm]]$trajectory, "static_dep")
b0 <- function(nm) fits[[nm]]$B0 / ref$ss3$ssb0
  • opal now takes the two SS3 settings AGE lacked: SS3’s lambda of 0 on parameter priors (data$lambdas$prior), and SS3’s generalised size compositions for the index on their own bins with SS3’s lambda of 0.51 (a second bin scheme through prep_lf_data(), weighted by lf lambdas). At SS3’s solution, opal’s predictions of those size compositions agree with SS3’s expected values.
  • Without priors, 20 selectivity parameters SS3 estimated are not identified, and AGE-NP and AGE-NP-SF hold them at their free estimates, which leaves the objective unchanged. AGE-NP then has a positive-definite Hessian; AGE-NP-SF does not. With the priors kept, AGE-SF passes opal_check().
  • From AGE’s estimates, B0 is 0.84 (AGE), 0.86 (AGE-NP), 0.91 (AGE-NP-SF) and 0.88 (AGE-SF) × SS3’s. Terminal depletion is 0.298, 0.309, 0.374 and 0.364, against SS3’s 0.399. The index size compositions move opal closest to SS3, with or without priors (AGE to AGE-SF, or AGE-NP to AGE-NP-SF). Removing the priors changes little at this optimum.
  • Started from SS3’s own solution, AGE-NP and AGE-NP-SF stop at an optimum with stock size close to SS3’s, but worse for opal’s likelihood. The remaining gap to SS3 is partly a question of which optimum each model is in, and partly the accepted structural differences (catch and survey timing, four quarterly catchabilities, unconstrained recruitment deviations).

The outputs in this article were computed with opal 0.1.1 (commit fd7efc2) by data-raw/generate-io-yft-matched-fits.R and data-raw/generate-io-yft-vignette-cache.R. SS3’s size compositions and lambdas were exported by code/rtmb/scripts/06-export-io-yft-sizefreq-for-opal.r in https://github.com/N-DucharmeBarth/wcpfc-bet-single-region.
